Nevertheless, anomalous Hall effect and quantum oscillations were recently found to coexist in magnetodiluted Bi$_2$Se$_3$-Co, presenting an excellent case study for investigating unconventional mechanisms underlying the anomalous Hall effect. Our analysis of Bi$_2$Se$_3$-Co sampling varying Co concentrations reveals that the hall effect is not caused by minimal magnetization or bulk magnetization, as shown by our measurements of magnetic susceptibility and magnetization along with magnetic scanning transmission microscopy. This hypothesis accounts for the linear relationship between the Hall coefficient and the square of magnetization seen in our data, as well as the variation in anomalous Hall angle displayed by Bi$_2$Se$_3$-Co.
